title: Mexican papel picado: advanced techniques
subtitle: Cutting tiered patterns, crossed borders, and fine details in tissue paper using a chisel and block
excerpt: Advanced papel picado uses a set of small steel chisels and a firm cutting block to cut multiple stacked layers of tissue paper at once. The chisel technique allows far finer detail than scissors: tiny star punches, crosshatched grids, and geometric borders that would be impossible to cut one layer at a time. This entry covers tiered border construction and the chisel toolkit, building on basic papel picado technique.
sourceNotes: Papel picado as a traditional Mexican craft is in the public domain. The chisel-cut technique is documented in craft ethnography of the San Salvador Huixcolotla region of Puebla, Mexico, where this technique has been practised commercially since at least the late nineteenth century. Description of tools and method based on published craft documentation.

glossaryTerms.definition: A small steel tool with a shaped cutting edge used to punch repeated motifs through multiple layers of tissue paper simultaneously. Chisel shapes include stars, circles, diamonds, crescents, and straight blades in various widths.
A papel picado border design using two or three repeated pattern rows at different scales, with the finest detail at the outer edge and progressively bolder elements toward the centre of the sheet.

The professional makers of San Salvador Huixcolotla cut 40 to 50 layers per stack: a beginner working alone should start with 8 to 12 layers and build up. The
pattern described below is the foundation of most traditional figural papel picado designs.

items.name: Tissue paper, in your chosen colours
items.notes: Mexican papel picado tissue is slightly heavier than gift wrap tissue (approximately 18 gsm). Stack 10 layers before cutting. Pre-fold and crease the edges of the stack to prevent shifting.

items.name: Papel picado chisels: star, circle, small blade, medium blade
items.notes: A starter set of 4 to 6 chisels is enough for border work. Keep them sharp: a blunt chisel tears the tissue rather than cutting cleanly.

items.name: Hardwood cutting block
items.notes: At least 30 mm thick. Softwood and cutting mats both compress under the chisel and produce torn rather than clean cuts. Hardwood is essential.

items.name: Craft knife and metal ruler
items.notes: For cutting the straight-edged elements of the border and the banner edges.

content.text: Stack 10 tissue paper sheets, alternating colours if making a multi-colour batch. Fold over 10 mm along all four edges and crease firmly to prevent the layers from shifting during cutting. Place the stack on the hardwood cutting block with the top (future decorative surface) face-down. Mark the border positions lightly in pencil on the back sheet.

Rule three parallel lines 8 mm, 15 mm, and 22 mm from the outer edge of the stack. These are the three border tiers. In the outer tier (8 mm from the edge), chisel a row of small star or circle motifs at 6 mm spacing. In the middle tier (8 to 15 mm from the edge), chisel a row of medium circle or diamond motifs at 10 mm spacing. In the inner tier (15 to 22 mm), cut a row of straight blade cuts at an angle to form a chevron or herringbone pattern. The combination of three different motif scales is what gives the tiered border its visual richness.

items.symptom: The chisel tears the tissue rather than cutting it cleanly
items.cause: The chisel edge is dull, or the cutting block is too soft.
items.fix: Sharpen the chisel on a fine whetstone or ceramic rod. If the problem is the block, replace with hardwood. A dull chisel on a soft block compresses and tears; a sharp chisel on hard wood cuts cleanly.

items.symptom: The layers shift during chisel cutting, so the pattern does not align between sheets
items.cause: The stack was not folded and creased at the edges before cutting.
items.fix: Fold and crease all four edges firmly before beginning. For stacks of more than 15 layers, a binder clip along each side (away from the cutting area) holds the layers together without interfering with the chisels.
